# lottie-render

> Render Lottie (After Effects / bodymovin) animations to MP4 video, frame by frame, using headless Chromium (Playwright) and FFmpeg. Usable as an npm library (`renderLottie()`) or as a self-hosted HTTP service.

Frames are captured deterministically via `goToAndStop`, not sampled off a real-time render loop, so output duration and frame count are exact. The render sandbox blocks all outbound network requests except local/data URIs (SSRF protection for untrusted Lottie input), and rejects animations exceeding configurable frame-count/dimension caps. MIT licensed.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/README.md): Installation, `renderLottie()` API reference, architecture, security notes, and the optional HTTP service.
- [DOCKER.md](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/DOCKER.md): Deploying the HTTP service with Docker.
- [Type definitions](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/src/types/index.ts): `RenderOptions`, `RenderResult`, `LottieJSON`, `LottieMetadata`.

## Examples

- [Library usage](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/test/e2e/library.test.ts): calling `renderLottie()` directly, with and without `outputPath`.
- [HTTP API usage](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/test/e2e/render.test.ts): calling `POST /api/render`.
- [Installed-package usage](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/test/e2e/package-install.test.ts): installing the published npm package and calling it from a separate process, including from TypeScript.
